why: Official pages that still state a figure the law has since changed. A passage containing one of these phrases is never given to the answer check, so the site cannot confirm a statement from it. Each entry names the law in force and where that was read. Added 2026-10-08 after the law exam: the site stated the Small Claims limit from before October 2025, read from the Superior Court's own guide. An entry with "phrase" withholds every passage containing it; an entry with "sentence" cuts that exact sentence out of the passage and keeps the rest.

entries.inForce: The Small Claims Court limit is $50,000: O. Reg. 626/00, s. 1 (1) (docs/sources/corpus/oreg-626-00-monetary-jurisdiction.txt), effective October 1, 2025 per ontario.ca, 'Small claims court: suing someone' (docs/sources/corpus/ontario-suing-someone-small-claims.txt).

entries.sentence: Effective October 1, 2025, the monetary jurisdiction of Small Claims Court will increase from $35,000 to $50,000 . The minimum appealable amount will increase from $3,500 to $5,000 .
entries.inForce: The change has happened: the limit is $50,000 (O. Reg. 626/00, s. 1 (1)) and the appeal amount $5,000 (s. 2). The rest of this page already states $50,000, so only the change notice is cut.
